problems.quote: The store keeps the money it predicted you'd never spend. The rest is still yours.
problems.fix: Implies part of the balance is no longer the holder's. It is: the card has no expiry and no balance-reducing fees. The store keeps it only if the holder never spends it. (Found in the final editorial read, after the automated checks passed.)

problems.quote: The store keeps the share it predicted you'd never spend.
problems.fix: Answer the question in its own words: 'the store keeps the money it predicted you'd never spend', then end on what the viewer can do.

problems.quote: Starbucks estimates how much money will never be redeemed.
problems.fix: Name the thing: the company calls that share breakage. One plain word the viewer can repeat.

problems.quote: It doesn't take that money from anyone.
problems.fix: Keep; it corrects the misconception directly. Tighten the second sentence so the timing is clear: a slice moves into sales each time someone else uses a card.
